summary: Akio Tanabe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Kyoto University, and became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 2015.

Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1930–1934), he served on its faculty, becoming a professor in 1968, and held visiting professorships at the University of Copenhagen and UC Berkeley.
Akira Hataya is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and later as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1962–1975) and also taught at Waseda and Rissho universities.

Akira Miyaji (born 1945) specialized in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Nagoya University (~1964–1991), he taught at Hirosaki University, became emeritus professor at Nagoya University, and served as director of the Ryukoku Museum.

Akira Momiyama (born 1953) is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1973–1977) and served as a professor at Saitama University from approximately 1996 to 2018.

Akira Mukai (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework and worked as an assistant at Hokkaido University before serving as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (~1981–2008).

Akira Omine (1929–2018) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University, under Kyoshi Takahama, and at Heidelberg University. He held professorships at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.

Akira Sadakata (born 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa, as well as the University of Paris, and served as a professor at Tokai University.

Akira Saito (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and at Australian National University, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (2000–2016).

Akira Shimada is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Daud Ali, having also studied under Rajeev Lochan, and became an associate professor at SUNY New Paltz in 2007.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1957–1962). He served on the faculty at Toyo University as an assistant and associate professor, and lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1965–1991) and taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University.
Akira Yamada (1922–2008) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947) under Tokuryu Yamauchi and held an academic post at Nanzan University.

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at ANU under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, and under Akira Hirakawa and Naoshiro Tsuji. He directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (1974–1996).

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at Taisho University, and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Akong Tulku Rinpoche (1939–2013) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He co-founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre in 1967 and served as its abbot.

Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and held a researcher position at Ghent University (both attested 2026).
Akshay Ramanlal Desai (1915–1994) was a scholar in history and archaeology who completed his studies at the University of Mumbai (~1935–1946) under the supervision of Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.

Alain Daniélou (1907–1994) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he became Professor of Musicology, and served as director of the French Institute of Pondicherry and the Adyar Library and Research Centre.
